## 1. The staff and the jinn  (`#the-staff-and-the-jinn`)

Cited ayat: 34:14

> **34:14** فَلَمَّا قَضَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَوْتَ مَا دَلَّهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَوْتِهِۦٓ إِلَّا دَآبَّةُ ٱلْأَرْضِ تَأْكُلُ مِنسَأَتَهُۥ فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلْجِنُّ أَن لَّوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْغَيْبَ مَا لَبِثُوا۟ فِى ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ

### Claims

**c1** (34:14): When God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff.

**c2** (34:14): When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment.

### One-minute summary

When God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff [c1]. When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah says that when God decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff [c1]. When he fell, it became clear to the jinn that, had they known the unseen, they would not have stayed in the humiliating punishment [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah gives a pair of moments: the decree of death with the creature eating the staff, and the falling after which it became clear to the jinn [c1][c2]. The statement about the unseen is made of the jinn: knowing the unseen would have kept them from the punishment [c2].

### Kids mode

The ayah says a small creature of the earth was eating a staff, and that was what showed his death [c1]. When he fell, the jinn saw that they did not know the unseen [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah teaches that knowledge of the unseen is not with the jinn [c2]. Another is that the ayah shows a death made known through an ordinary creature and an ordinary object [c1].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: who is meant; the ayah does not name him, and the inventory title identifies him from the verses before this one, which are outside the verses cited here.
- Not established: how long he remained as he was, what the staff was, or what the creature of the earth was.
- Not established: what work the jinn were doing, or how they came to know the matter; the ayah says only that it became clear to them when he fell.
- Not established: who is meant by them in the first clause; the ayah does not say who was not shown his death.
